subject: English
question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 'May' Day or International Workers Day is observed on May 1 all over the world today to commemorate the historical struggle and sacrifices of the working people to establish an eight-hour working day. It is a public holiday in almost all the countries of the world. Since the Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries in Europe and the US, the workers in mills and factories had been working a long shift, fourteen or even more hours a day. On May 1st in 1886, inspired by the trade unions(, half of the workers at the McCormic Harvester Company in Chicago went on strike demanding an eight-hour working day. Two days later about 6000 workers brought out a rally addressed by the labour leaders. Suddenly about 200 policemen attacked them with clubs and revolvers. One striker was killed instantly, five or six others were seriously wounded and many of them were badly injured. The events of May 1, 1886 is a reminder that workers will continue to be exploited until they stand up and speak out to gain better working conditions, better pay and better lives. [Unit-3; Lesson-2] The world observes the May Day after a long struggle and great (a) ⎯. For this, memorable struggle workers now can enjoy an eight hours workday. May 1st has been (b) ⎯ Board & Test Questions : First Paper as a public holiday in (c) ⎯ all the countries of the world. The workers had to work (d) ⎯ hours or more a day before the may 1st (e) ⎯. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose was born in Bikrampur, Dhaka on November 30,1858. Bose passed the Entrance Examination (SSC) in 1875 from Hare School and got into St Xavier's College, Kolkata. He received a bachelor degree from the University of Kolkata in 1879. He did BSC degree from the University of London in 1884. He reterned to India in 1885 and joined Presidency College as an Assistant Professor of Physics. Bose wrote a book Response in the living and Non living, in 1902 and in the book he proved that plants are sensitive to heat, cold, light noise and other external stimuli just like human being. The discovery made him world famous. He passed away on November 23, 1937.
